patterns_found.visual_evidence: The mobile sketch shows a compact header with a boxed three-line icon at the top right, a standard hamburger trigger for collapsed navigation.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Tapping the icon should open and close the primary navigation panel. The current page should be indicated within the revealed menu if navigation items are present there.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not show whether the menu opens as a dropdown below the header, an off-canvas drawer, or a full-screen overlay.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: Both sketches place a persistent top header/navigation bar spanning the width of the page, visually separated from content by a horizontal rule, implying a fixed site header.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: The top navigation/header should likely remain fixed while scrolling so branding and navigation stay accessible across the long content page.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not explicitly show scrolling states, so fixed-on-scroll versus simply top-positioned at page load is inferred.

sketch_notes: The sketches imply a mostly static informational page with low JavaScript complexity. The only clearly interactive requirement is responsive navigation: mobile uses a collapsed hamburger menu, while both viewports suggest a persistent top navigation/header that may need sticky behavior during scroll. No forms, tabs, accordions, modals, search, pagination, or dynamic loading controls are visually indicated; the rest appears to be straightforward static content and lists.
